procedure.step: Register factory with the ministry prior to applying for a Certificate of Origin. Factory must be located outside a free zone, hold a MoIAT industrial licence, and obtain a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added.

Apply for 'Certificate of Origin for India' through the ministry portal (eservices.moec.gov.ae) or smart app prior to, at, or within 5 working days of export. Submit commercial invoice and proof of factory registration, and pay the fee (AED 50 for AED 100,000 invoice).
Receive the approved Certificate of Origin, valid for 12 months from issue for a single import shipment into India.
Indian importer claims CEPA preferential rate upon filing the bill of entry, maintains origin documents under CAROTAR 2020, and uploads the certificate to e-Sanchit.
Retain all origin records and detailed cost breakdowns for at least 5 years from the end of the year of certificate issuance.

caveats.note: The symbol '+' in the product-specific rule is read as 'and', requiring both CTSH and VA 45% checks to pass.
Origin qualification relies on the exporter's declaration regarding UAE final manufacture and non-minimal operations.

Duty savings are estimated on Basic Customs Duty (BCD) using the declared shipment value. India charges duty on assessable (CIF) import value. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and anti-dumping duties still apply.
Factory registration requires the facility to be located outside a free zone; free-zone factories are likely not eligible.
